newsitem.title: FRANCE: France air cargo task force to visit Latam and US.
newsitem.headline: France air cargo task force to visit Latam and US.

text.p: The Paris airports authority, Aeroports de Paris (ADP), said it will send an air cargo task force on missions to Latin America and the U.S. in the autumn.

"The main aim of these trips is to promote the Paris airports as a gateway for air cargo in addressing airfreight forwarding agents and other industry professionals as well as shippers," a spokesman for the ADP's freight marketing department told Reuters.
The task force will include representatives from ADP, Air France Cargo, the French cargo agents' association SNAGFA and French Customs, the spokesman said.
Between September 1-5, the task force will visit Sao Paulo, Buenos Aires and Santiago, he added. All three are served with scheduled cargo services by Air France.

"This will be the task force's first trip to Latin America, a region which generates relatively minor air cargo volumes in relation to North America and the Far East, but whose rate of growth is among the strongest in the industry," added the spokesman.

Following the Air Cargo Americas trade fair at the end of October in Miami (October 29-31), the ADP task force will begin a five-day mission to the U.S. (November 3-7) taking in Miami, Atlanta and Houston.

"Atlanta and Houston are respectively the hubs of Delta and Continental Airlines and the two carriers' potential co-operation with Air France on freight traffic, following their passenger alliance (which started on Monday with the French flag carrier), will provide the backdrop to the task force's visit," the spokesman said.
Air France operates scheduled cargo services to Miami and Houston and ad hoc full-freighters to Atlanta.
